highlights_headline: SkiaSharp 4.151.0 adds a new Vulkan Silk.NET package, expands platform support, and syncs Skia m151 bug fixes.
highlights_body: This release introduces the `SkiaSharp.Vulkan.Silk.NET` integration package, brings font rendering to Nano Server via FreeType, and expands verified platform support to Azure Linux, Alpine/musl, and Nano Server containers. The bundled Skia engine picks up upstream m151 bug fixes.

bullets.lead: Skia m151 upstream bug fixes merged
bullets.detail: The bundled renderer is updated with the latest upstream chrome/m151 patches, keeping SkiaSharp aligned with the current stable Skia engine.
A dedicated NuGet package for Vulkan GPU backend integration via Silk.NET is now available, making it straightforward to wire up a Vulkan surface without manual P/Invoke.

bullets.lead: CoTaskMem pixel-buffer leak fixed in SKImage.Create
bullets.detail: A native memory leak in the raster-image failure path of `SKImage.Create` was plugged — the CoTaskMem buffer is now freed correctly when Skia rejects the pixel data.
The null-terminated fast path in `GetEncodedText` no longer allocates an intermediate string, reducing GC pressure in text-heavy rendering loops.
The uniform-name lookup map is now sized to the known uniform count upfront, eliminating repeated rehashing on first access for effects with many uniforms.

bullets.lead: Font rendering on Nano Server via FreeType
bullets.detail: Nano Server's stripped GDI environment previously prevented font loading; SkiaSharp now routes font access through FreeType on that platform, fixing text rendering for Windows container workloads.

bullets.lead: Verified support for Azure Linux, Alpine/musl, and Nano Server
bullets.detail: Containerized CI legs now confirm that SkiaSharp runs correctly on Azure Linux, Alpine (musl libc), and Windows Nano Server, giving these targets the same tested-and-verified status as the mainline platforms.

contributor_summaries.jeffska: Enabled FreeType-based font loading on Windows Nano Server, fixing long-standing text rendering failures in GDI-less container environments
